title: Kafka Fundamentals
interviewAnswer: Kafka is a distributed event log. Producers write records to partitioned topics; consumers read offsets, often in consumer groups for parallelism and fault tolerance.
why: Kafka appears in data-engineering and ML-platform interviews because it cleanly separates event producers from many downstream consumers.
intuition: A topic is split into partitions. Producers append records; consumers read records by offset. Consumer groups divide partitions among members so processing can scale horizontally.
deepDive: Kafka is a durable distributed log rather than a simple message queue. Ordering is guaranteed within a partition, not across an entire multi-partition topic. Delivery semantics depend on producer, broker and consumer processing/commit behavior.
math: Key relationship: one partition is actively consumed by at most one consumer in the same consumer group at a time.

commonMistakes: Saying Kafka itself performs arbitrary stream analytics—that is typically handled by stream processors/consumers.
Confusing consumer groups with broadcast to independent applications.
followUps: What happens when a consumer fails?
production: Monitor lag, throughput, partition balance, broker health and schema compatibility. Choose partition keys carefully because they define ordering and load distribution.
workedExample: In a radiation-monitoring pipeline, a producer publishes measurements to Kafka while a Flink job consumes and processes them independently.
